population_note: UN WPP 2024 medium variant (~9.7 bn); not re-fetched here (evidence P01). Per-capita values scale as 1/population.

final_energy_GJ_per_cap_yr.derivation: Global 1.5C-compatible final energy in 2050 divided by 9.66 bn. low = LED 245 EJ (Grubler 2018, E02); central = IEA NZE 2023 343 EJ (E06); high = AR6 WG3 C1 median 410 EJ (E03; C1 p5-p95 325-540 EJ = 33.6-55.9 GJ). 2C reference: C3 median 448 EJ (E04). Floor: Millward-Hopkins 2020 149 EJ (E01).

co2_t_per_cap_yr.derivation: low: 1.5C 50% budget = 130 GtCO2 from start of 2025 (Forster 2025, C08); a linear decline from 42.2 Gt/yr reaches zero by about 2031, so net CO2 in 2050 is <= 0 and residual emissions need CDR. central: AR6 C1 energy and industry CO2 index in 2050 = 8% of 2020 (E03), with 2025 total 42.2 Gt used as proxy base = 3.4 Gt, which is 0.35 t gross (net about 0). high: 2C 67% budget 870 Gt from 2025 (C11); linear decline to net zero in 2066 leaves 16.6 Gt in 2050 = 1.72 t (50%: 1050 Gt, net zero 2075, 2.17 t). O'Neill 2018 2C boundary 1.61 t (G01). today: 42.2 Gt / ~8.2 bn.

cropland_m2_per_cap.derivation: low: EAT-Lancet 2019 cropland boundary 13 M km2 (F04) / 9.66 bn. central: no net cropland expansion, so 2021 cropland of 1,580 Mha (F07) / 9.66 bn. This matches the EAT-Lancet 2025 land rule of no conversion of intact land and total agricultural land below 48 M km2 (F03). high: EAT-Lancet 2025 healthy-diet scenario ensemble with cropland +11% vs 2020 (model range -3% to +42%), offset by -11% grazing land (total agricultural land -7%) (F05). today: FAO 0.2 ha/cap (2021).

material_footprint_t_per_cap_yr.derivation: low: Bringezu 2015 corridor lower bound 3 t (M04). central: 50 Gt/yr global cap (the common denominator in O'Neill 2018, M02) / 9.66 bn = 5.2 t, close to Bringezu's 5 t. high: IRP 6-8 t upper bound (M03) and Dittrich 8 t (M05). today: 39 kg/person/day x 365 (M01) = 14.2 t.

unira_40GJ_test.verdict_1p5C: Inside the AR6 C1 range (325-540 EJ) and below the C1 median, but 13% above IEA NZE. So 40 GJ for all is compatible with 1.5C-class energy pathways (limited or temporary overshoot) only if solar+wind build-out reaches about 1.3 TW/yr by around 2030. That is about 1.9 times the 2025 record of 669 GW (510 PV + 159 wind), with electricity at about 50% of final energy and fossil CO2 near net zero by 2050. With only 130 GtCO2 left at 50% (about 3 years of emissions), no energy level avoids at least a temporary overshoot of 1.5C.
unira_40GJ_test.verdict_2C: Compatible. 386 EJ is below the C3 median of 448 EJ; the 2C 67% budget (870 Gt from 2025) allows a linear decline to net zero by about 2066. This works with build-out at the IRENA tripling pace (about 1.1 TW/yr all renewables).

buildout_required_solar_wind_GW_per_yr.derivation: NZE 2030 additions of 820 PV + 320 wind (E07), scaled by 386.4/343 EJ. A first-order scaling, not a model run.

food_fit_2470kcal_9p7bn: Conditional yes. EAT-Lancet 2025 finds a healthy diet for 9.6 bn within boundaries at 2,400 kcal intake. This requires the diet shift (ruminant meat -33%), food loss and waste halved, and 7-10% extra productivity. 2,470 kcal is +3% above that reference, inside the stated uncertainty, but only with a planetary-health diet composition. A comfortable diet at today's composition and waste does not fit, because cropland and nitrogen are already over the boundaries.
caveats: AR6 C1 pathways start from 2020 budgets; post-2020 emissions have used about 75% of the 50% 1.5C budget, so C1 final-energy levels now imply faster decarbonisation or more CDR.
Scenario totals assume unequal distribution; equal 40 GJ means large cuts in high-income countries (see v65).
The material targets are an immature literature (O'Neill 2018 says so explicitly); the energy-transition minerals are not separated out.
Values marked partial/no in evidence.csv (F04 range, M03-M05 primaries, C14, P01) were not read in primary text.
